tasks.title: TDD: Port stream filter — stream processing
tasks.description:
Implement the processStream() function in src/stream-filter.ts that reads stream-json lines and writes formatted output. Write tests first.

processStream should accept a readable stream (or async iterable of lines) and a writable stream, plus options for dependencies (narration, ntfy — leave as no-ops for now, task 3 will fill those in).

Event handling (match the Python main loop exactly):
1. Skip empty lines. Parse each line as JSON; if parse fails, pass through as-is.
2. type='system' + subtype='init': print '[init] <model> | <permissionMode>' in dim.
3. type='assistant': iterate content blocks. For tool_use blocks, print '  > <fmtTool(block)>'. For text blocks, if RALPH_TRUNCATE_TEXT is true (default), show first line truncated to 80 chars. If false, show full text indented. Use YELLOW color for text.
4. type='result': print fmtResult(event).

Design for testability: use string/buffer streams in tests. Read RALPH_TRUNCATE_TEXT from env (or accept as option).

All output should be flushed immediately (write with newlines).

tasks.title: TDD: Port stream filter — narration and ntfy
tasks.description:
Add narration socket forwarding and ntfy push notifications to the stream filter. Write tests first.

1. sendToNarrate(text, socketPath): Forward text to a Unix domain socket. Best-effort, non-blocking. Skip if socketPath is empty, socket doesn't exist, or text is empty. Use 1s timeout. Catch all errors silently.
2. sendNtfy(message, topic, opts?): POST to https://ntfy.sh/<topic>. Support optional Title, Priority, Tags headers. 5s timeout. Best-effort, catch all errors.
3. Wire into processStream via injectable options (e.g., { narrate?: (text: string) => void, ntfy?: (msg: string, opts?) => void }) so tests can mock these.
4. Narration triggers (match Python):
   - On system/init with RALPH_TASK_CONTEXT: narrate 'Starting work on: <context>' and ntfy same.
   - On assistant text blocks: forward text (prepend task context if set), truncated to 1000 chars.
   - On result: narrate and ntfy a summary with status/turns/duration. Use different ntfy tags/priority for success vs error.

Test with mock functions passed as options. Also test sendToNarrate with a real Unix socket server in the test, and sendNtfy with a mock HTTP intercept if feasible.

tasks.title: TDD: Port init command — interactive prompts
tasks.description:
Add interactive prompts for ralph.json configuration to src/commands/init.ts. Write tests first.

Read lib/ralph_init.sh to understand all prompts. Use Node's built-in readline/promises for interactive input. Key behaviors:

1. Prompt for each ralph.json field with sensible defaults (auto-detected where possible):
   - Project name (default: directory basename)
   - Health check command (auto-detect from package.json/Cargo.toml/Makefile)
   - Test command
   - Implementation file name (default: IMPLEMENTATION.md)
   - Model preference (default: opus)
   - Max iterations (default: 25)
   - And other fields from the shell version
2. Boolean prompts: show [Y/n] when default is true, [y/N] when default is false. Accept y/yes/n/no case-insensitive, empty = default.
3. Re-init support: if ralph.json already exists, load its values as defaults for all prompts.
4. Write ralph.json with the collected values.

Extract prompt helpers as testable functions. For testing, create a mock readline interface that returns predetermined answers. Test default values, boolean parsing, re-init default loading, and final JSON output.

tasks.title: TDD: Port init command — instructions.md and narration hooks
tasks.description:
Add optional instructions.md creation and narration hooks installation to the init command. Write tests first.

1. instructions.md: After ralph.json prompts, ask if the user wants to create .ralph/instructions.md. If yes, create the file with a template/placeholder, then open it in $EDITOR (fall back to vi). If $EDITOR launch fails, just print the path.
2. Narration hooks: Ask if the user wants to install Claude Code narration hooks. If yes, create .claude/hooks/ directory and install the hook scripts (match the shell version's behavior for what hooks are installed).
3. Display 'Next steps' message at the end showing what was created and suggesting next commands (ralph plan, etc.).

Wire everything together into a top-level runInit() function that calls initCoreFiles, runs prompts, then handles instructions.md and hooks.

For testing: mock $EDITOR and child_process.spawnSync. Test the prompt flow, file creation, and next-steps output. Use temp directories.

tasks.title: TDD: Port summarize command — system prompt building
tasks.notes: Created src/commands/summarize.ts with buildContext(), buildClaudeMdPruning(), and buildSummarizePrompt(). All match shell logic in ralph_summarize.sh exactly. 14 tests in test/commands/summarize.test.ts, all pass. buildContext() computes relative path from projectRoot to completedTasksPath using path.relative(). buildSummarizePrompt() opts includes projectRoot, projectName, implFile, completedTasksPath, claudeMdPattern — caller must supply these from config.
tasks.description:
Port the system prompt building logic from lib/ralph_summarize.sh to src/commands/summarize.ts. Write tests first in test/commands/summarize.test.ts.

Read lib/ralph_summarize.sh fully to understand the prompt construction. Key responsibilities:

1. Build context string: 'Updating from the central task list.' + completed tasks file reference if it exists.
2. Detect existing implementation file: if present, instruct 'update in place'; if not, instruct 'create from scratch'.
3. Build the full system prompt including:
   - Role/purpose description for the summarize agent
   - CLAUDE.md pruning instructions (the agent should focus on implementation details, not repeat CLAUDE.md)
   - Project context (implementation file path, completed tasks path)
   - The existing/not-existing note
4. Read RALPH_IMPL_FILE from config (default: IMPLEMENTATION.md).

Export a buildSummarizePrompt(opts) function that returns the prompt string. Export helpers for detecting files and building context.

Test prompt content for various scenarios: fresh project, existing implementation file, with/without completed tasks.

tasks.title: TDD: Port summarize command — claude agent spawning
tasks.description:
Add claude agent spawning with stream-json output to the summarize command. Write tests first.

Implement runSummarize() in src/commands/summarize.ts:
1. Call buildSummarizePrompt() to get the system prompt.
2. Build the user prompt (the actual instruction to update/create the implementation file).
3. Spawn `claude -p '<user_prompt>' --append-system-prompt '<system_prompt>' --output-format stream-json --model sonnet --dangerously-skip-permissions` as a child process.
4. Pipe stdout through the TS stream filter (processStream from src/stream-filter.ts).
5. Implement timeout handling: 15 minutes default, configurable. Use AbortController + setTimeout or a process kill timer. Print a message if timed out.
6. After completion, check if the implementation file exists and report line count, or report 'was not created'.
7. Print banner header/footer matching the shell version's style.

For testing: mock child_process.spawn to return a fake process with controllable stdout. Verify the correct claude CLI arguments are constructed. Test timeout behavior. Test result reporting for both success and 'not created' cases.

tasks.title: Wire init and summarize into Commander, update fallbacks
tasks.description:
Register init and summarize as native Commander commands and remove them from shell fallback maps.

Changes needed:

1. src/index.ts:
   - Import runInit from ./commands/init and runSummarize from ./commands/summarize
   - Add 'init' command: program.command('init').description('Initialize Ralph in the current project').action(() => runInit(...))
   - Add 'summarize' command: program.command('summarize').description('Update implementation documentation').action(() => runSummarize(...))
   - Remove 'init' and 'summarize' from SHELL_FALLBACK_COMMANDS array
   - Note: init needs special handling — it should work WITHOUT an existing .ralph/ dir (setupProjectContext may need adjustment since findProjectRoot looks for .ralph/)

2. src/commands/fallback.ts:
   - Remove 'summarize' from COMMAND_SCRIPT_MAP
   - Remove 'init' from BIN_RALPH_COMMANDS

3. Update tests:
   - test/index.test.ts: update SHELL_FALLBACK_COMMANDS expectations, add tests for init and summarize command registration
   - test/commands/fallback.test.ts: update expectations for removed entries
   - Verify RALPH_FORCE_SHELL=1 still delegates everything to shell (existing test should still pass)

Run the full test suite: bun test

tasks.title: Verify bun build --compile produces working binary
tasks.description:
Build the compiled binary and verify all commands work correctly.

1. Run: bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile dist/ralph
2. Test the compiled binary:
   - dist/ralph --version → should print version
   - dist/ralph status → should work (in a project with .ralph/)
   - dist/ralph edit → should work
   - dist/ralph logs → should work
   - dist/ralph init → should run interactive prompts (test in a temp dir)
   - dist/ralph summarize → should attempt to spawn claude (will fail without claude CLI, but verify it gets to the spawn step)
   - dist/ralph plan → should fall back to shell
   - dist/ralph run → should fall back to shell
3. Test RALPH_FORCE_SHELL=1 dist/ralph status → should delegate to shell
4. If any command fails in compiled form, investigate and fix the issue.

Run bun test first to make sure all tests pass, then build and do manual verification.
